newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen weighted ahead of benchmark shift.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen weighted ahead of benchmark shift.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to be top-heavy and to move in a limited range on Wednesday amid a lack of fresh factors, with a shift in the benchmark from June to September assured after the volume of September rose above June in London overnight.
Both contracts rose slightly in London after the yen gained strength as a safe-haven currency amid EMU turmoil, but this is not expected to have much impact in Tokyo.
Traders said that of far more importance are moves in Tokyo stocks, which have been strong this week, with rises towards 21,000 making a downside try likely.
The range today for June is expected to be from 123.60 to 124.10, with support at 123.50 and resistance at 124.20.
In London, the September contract was sold as low as 122.31 before short-covering emerged to lead it higher.
But trade overall is expected to be range-bound, with few fresh factors until U.S. employment data on Friday, which may have an impact, depending on how U.S. Treasury bonds respond.

"Barring statements from Japanese officials, we can look for a rather quiet day, as the market is already turning its eye to the next Bank of Japan 'tankan' on June 25," one dealer at a securities firm said.
